newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela's Banco Latino gets at least 15 bidders.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela's Banco Latino gets at least 15 bidders.

text.p: At least 15 groups, both foreign and local, have shown interest in bidding for Venezuela's leasing company Arfinan as a result of the restructuring of Banco Latino, the bank's president Rolando Salcedo said.

"There is definitely a lot of interest in the bank," he told Reuters in a telephone interview on Tuesday. "So far, six foreign groups and nine local ones have expressed interest in taking part in the bidding," he said.
Half of the domestic entities are banks, he said, while the foreign investors are from Europe, one from the United States, another from Chile and one from Ecuador.

The auction of Banco Latino, whose collapse in January 1994 sparked an unprecedented, two-year crisis in the Venezuelan banking sector, is scheduled for December 16 at a price of about 22 billion bolivars ($47 million).
The privatization process began on November 4 with the opening of the "data room" of Arfinan. It allowed interested bidders to access information on the bank's financial statements and structure.
Part of the Latino group, Arfinan will be converted into a commercial bank with initial capital of 1.2 billion bolivars ($2.6 million). Banco Latino as en entity is set to disappear.
Salcedo said the bank hoped to complete this week the process of access to a web site on the Internet for interested bidders at a cost of $5,000.

Next month's auction will include Banco Latino's remaining 46 branches, five drive-in banks, an automatic teller network of 45 sites and deposits of some 135 billion bolivars ($282 million) from about 400,000 clients.
